title: Praxis Retail - Pilot golden set & load/KPI scoping kickoff
summary: Kickoff for a 4-week pilot to validate quality and load for Praxis Retail's checkout and returns assistant. Agreed on golden-set definition, high-level success metrics (format/safety pass rates and latency SLOs), sample size for regression and load targets. Action items: Redwood to share benchmark template and golden-set spreadsheet; Praxis to provide anonymized sample prompts and an infra contact for VPC peering; schedule benchmarking window in 2 weeks.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jun Park (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen (Praxis Head of ML), Diego Ramos (Platform), Priya Menon (PM), Aaron Holt (CTO)

Summary (auto): kickoff for pilot scoping to define golden prompts, regression plan, load targets, and timeline. Focus on checkout/returns assistant flows and hallucination guards.

---
00:00 Lena Ortiz: hey everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna run about 45 to 60 minutes, uh quick intros and then jump into the quality and load plan, sound good?
00:18 Maya Chen: yep that's great, thanks Lena, uh Maya here. We're especially focused on hallucinations in the returns flow and strict formatting for instructions to our ops team.
00:30 Samir Patel: great, Samir from Redwood on the SE side. we'll cover golden set, scoring, regression cadence, and then sizing for throughput and latency targets. quick check: do we have any restricted data concerns up front?
00:45 Diego Ramos: Diego here, platform. we'll scrub PII before we hand over but, uh, want the infra notes for V P C peering and a service account.
00:58 Lena Ortiz: noted. Jun from our CSM will help with onboarding and timeline coordination.
01:10 Jun Park: hi all.
01:20 Priya Menon: priya here, PM, main success metric is reduced agent handle time and fewer manual escalations — so we care about accuracy and format.

02:05 Samir Patel: ok first, success criteria — let's put numbers on paper. high-level proposal: format/structure pass rate >= 97% on golden-set, hallucination rate < 2% on regression bench, semantic acceptance (business) >= 90% on golden prompts, and latency p50 < 350ms and p95 < 800ms in pilot env. are those in the ballpark?
02:35 Aaron Holt: 97% format feels ambitious but reasonable if we lock the prompt templates; for latency can we get 200 rps? our peak checkout concurrency is roughly 150 requests per second for the assistant.
02:52 Samir Patel: 150 rps target noted. we usually recommend starting with a lower concurrency baseline and then run step tests: 50, 100, 150, 200. caching and continuous batching will affect tail latency; also KV cache (sometimes transcribed as K V cash) effectiveness depends on prefix reuse.
03:20 Maya Chen: our common prefixes are around 30% reuse for order-status flows, lower on returns.
03:32 Samir Patel: good to know. for golden prompts — we suggest three buckets: canonical happy-path (500 items), edge cases (200 items), and safety/hallucination checks (200 items). that gives a 900-item golden set to drive scoring and regression.
03:56 Diego Ramos: 900 total seems fine. will Praxis curate those? or do you expect Redwood to help annotate?
04:10 Lena Ortiz: collaboration — Praxis curates and we help label acceptance (pass/fail) for a subset if you want. we'll provide a template CSV and guidelines.
04:25 Priya Menon: we need structured output — the assistant returns JSON with fields A, B, and C; if formatting is off that triggers escalation. style must be strict.
04:40 Samir Patel: perfect, we'll add format checks: JSON validity, required keys, enum values. these are binary checks in the regression harness.
05:00 Samir Patel: hallucination checks are trickier — we recommend a mix of automated heuristics (entity hallucination detectors) and human annotations for a random sample. accept threshold we proposed was < 2% hallucination on the golden-set.
05:20 Maya Chen: how do you define hallucination? sometimes the model gives plausible but incorrect order numbers.
05:30 Samir Patel: good question — for this pilot let's define hallucination as any assertion about external state (order id, refund amount, inventory) that contradicts the source-of-truth snapshot we provide; automated check for format plus human verify for sampled cases.
05:52 Aaron Holt: makes sense. scoring approach - are you doing weighted scores?
06:02 Samir Patel: yes we propose a composite score: 40% format/structure, 30% semantic correctness, 20% hallucination, 10% latency penalty. each item in golden-set gets scored and we compute pass rates and a mean composite score.
06:20 Priya Menon: do you provide per-prompt feedback or an aggregate dashboard?
06:28 Jun Park: we'll provide per-prompt logs and aggregated dashboards in Redwood Console; for the pilot we'll include traces and token-level cost breakdown on samples.
06:40 Maya Chen: ok good. on regression cadence — what's realistic? weekly? daily?
06:46 Samir Patel: for a short pilot, we'd run nightly regression against the golden-set and full regression weekly. for production you'd want nightly smoke and weekly full.
07:00 Diego Ramos: for load testing, we'll need a window where we can run synthetic traffic against a dedicated test pool. what's your preferred approach?
07:12 Samir Patel: two options: hosted benchmark run on Redwood's test pool (fastest) or spin up a dedicated test cluster in Praxis V P C — we prefer dedicated for realistic network and VPC peering checks.
07:28 Lena Ortiz: trade-offs: hosted is quicker, dedicated gives accurate p95 and networking behavior. for enterprise customers we often do a combined approach: baseline on hosted then final run in customer VPC.
07:42 Aaron Holt: we prefer the combined approach. Diego will provision the test VPC.
07:50 Diego Ramos: got it. I'll put in the ticket after this call.
08:00 Samir Patel: sizing — to reproduce 150 rps with realistic token sizes, what’s your average prompt length and response length?
08:08 Maya Chen: average prompt is ~120 tokens, response about 180 tokens. some returns flows generate longer responses up to 400 tokens.
08:20 Samir Patel: good detail. we'll use that distribution in the benchmark. estimate GPU utilization and per-token costs accordingly; we'll share expected slot sizing in the template.
08:34 Priya Menon: one other concern, we need RBAC and audit logs since these are customer data touch points.
08:42 Jun Park: Redwood Private supports audit logs, K M S integrations, and fine-grained RBAC — we'll send the SOC 2 and security pack after the call.
08:55 Maya Chen: do you support S S O via SAML?
09:00 Jun Park: yes SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning — we'll include setup docs.
09:10 Samir Patel: back to the scoring: do we threshold on composite score or per-dimension pass rates? we recommend both: composite minimum 85 and no individual dimension below 75 except latency which is soft.
09:28 Aaron Holt: that seems fine. what about regression flakiness? sometimes model updates cause variability.
09:36 Samir Patel: we track regression deltas and set regression alert thresholds — e.g., if hallucination increases by >1% absolute or format pass drops by >3% we open a regression ticket and revert to the fallback model.
09:52 Lena Ortiz: fallback policies — we'll discuss canary and automatic fallback to a lower-latency or smaller model if errors spike. add that to the runbook.
10:05 Diego Ramos: curious about quantization/accuracy trade-offs — will you test int8 variants?
10:12 Samir Patel: yes we can include quantized variants in the benchmark and report accuracy deltas. often int8 is very close for these tasks but we'll validate.
10:25 Maya Chen: timing — you mentioned a 4-week pilot earlier, can you break down tasks?
10:32 Lena Ortiz: proposed plan: week 0 (this week) — data prep and infra; week 1 — integration and baseline runs; week 2 — targeted quality tuning (golden-set regression nightly); week 3 — load ramps and final acceptance, plus a results review and next-steps decision.
10:50 Priya Menon: who signs off at Praxis? me and Maya together, and Aaron for ops sign-off.
10:58 Lena Ortiz: great — we'll capture sign-off criteria in the doc.
11:10 Samir Patel: instrumentation — please ensure your test data has a snapshot of source-of-truth for orders so hallucination checks can run automatically.
11:20 Diego Ramos: we'll provide a small read-only snapshot in S3 for the duration of the tests.
11:30 Jun Park: will you need tokenization details or prompt templates to be fixed?
11:36 Maya Chen: yes we'll share prompt templates — some use structured system messages that must be preserved.
11:44 Samir Patel: ok we'll honor system messages and show token delta effects in the benchmark.
11:52 Aaron Holt: any legal/NDAs to sign before we exchange sample data?
11:57 Lena Ortiz: we have an NDA template; Jun will send it. once signed, we'll accept the dataset upload.
12:05 Jun Park: I'll send SOC 2 + security pack and the NDA link after the call.
12:14 Priya Menon: what about timeline for the baseline report?
12:18 Samir Patel: target by 2027-11-15 for the baseline numbers; final report end of pilot 2027-11-26.
12:30 Maya Chen: ok sounds good. one last question — do you provide human-in-the-loop labeling tools or do we use our own?
12:38 Samir Patel: Redwood can augment with labeling support for the pilot; we can do an initial annotation pass for 200 samples to seed the regression. we'll include that as an optional line item.
12:52 Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone. quick recap and explicit next steps: Lena to send template and spreadsheet, Maya to upload samples, Diego to provision VPC, Samir to run baseline and share results. mid pilot check-in scheduled.
13:20 Aaron Holt: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
13:30 End call.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-words (e.g., K V cash for KV cache, S A S L) and speaker overlaps. Shared artifacts referenced: benchmark_template.csv (link placeholder), golden_set_template.xlsx (link placeholder), security_pack.pdf (link placeholder).

- Maya Chen: upload anonymized dataset (1k prompts + 200 edge cases) (due 2027-11-05)
